title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 164
paragraphs: Such was the answer the Pythian priestess gave to Arcesilaus. He, taking with him those in Samos, returned to Cyrene. Once he had seized power, he forgot the oracle's saying and set about exacting punishments from those of the opposing faction for having driven him out. Of these, some escaped the country altogether, but some Arcesilaus got into his hands and sent off to Cyprus to be put to death. These were driven off course to Cnidus, and the Cnidians rescued them and sent them away to Thera. Other Cyrenaeans, however, had taken refuge in a great tower belonging to a private citizen named Aglomachus, and Arcesilaus burned them alive by piling up brushwood around it. After the deed he realized that this was what the oracle had meant when the Pythian priestess forbade him, if he found the jars in the furnace, to heat them fiercely; and he deliberately kept away from the city of Cyrene, fearing the death foretold by the oracle and supposing that Cyrene was the place washed around by water. He had as wife a kinswoman of his own, the daughter of the king of Barca whose name was Alazeir. He went to him; and certain Barcans, together with some of the Cyrenaean exiles, noticing him walking in the marketplace, killed him, and killed his father-in-law Alazeir along with him. So Arcesilaus, whether willingly or unwillingly, by misreading the oracle fulfilled his own fate.
